claim_text: Ochsner Health says an unauthorized party accessed two employee user accounts in its Microsoft environment on Sept 18 to 21, 2026, and downloaded files from one of them
summary: Ochsner's notice says an outside forensic firm found two employee accounts were accessed without authorization from Sept 18 to 21 and files in one were downloaded. It says the incident was limited to its Microsoft environment.
detail: This is the company's account on its own website, repeated by KLFY, WWL-TV, The Advocate, WDSU and KTBS. Ochsner does not say how the accounts were accessed or who did it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, Ochsner's own notice, says it, and several independent outlets report the same statement.
notes: The notice calls the person an "unauthorized party" and an "unauthorized actor." It does not use the word "hack" or "cyberattack."

claim_text: Ochsner says it learned of the incident on Oct 1, determined on Nov 18 that specific information was accessed, and began notifying people on Nov 19
summary: The notice dates three steps: Oct 1 (learned of a data incident and secured the accounts), Nov 18 (determined specific information was accessed) and Nov 19 (began notifying individuals). Formal letters are to follow “in the coming weeks.”
detail: The gap between the September access and the November notices is Ochsner's own timeline. The notice does not say why the review took until Nov 18.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ochsner's own notice (Tier 1), with outlets reporting the same dates.

claim_text: Ochsner says the files "may include" names, demographic information, Social Security numbers and health information, and it varies by person
summary: Ochsner says the information in the files varies by individual. It is offering one year of free credit monitoring to people whose Social Security numbers were involved.
detail: “May include” is Ochsner's wording. It has not said how many people, or which kinds of information, apply to whom.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ochsner's own notice (Tier 1) says it, and outlets report it.
notes: Confirmed that Ochsner says this. Which people are affected is not established (c008).

claim_text: Ochsner patient care, its Epic health record system, MyOchsner or MyChart were disrupted by the incident
summary: Ochsner says there has been no disruption to patient care, its electronic health record (Epic, MyOchsner/MyChart) or any of its systems as a result of the incident.
detail: This rests on Ochsner's own statement, which KLFY, WWL-TV, KTBS and WDSU report. We found no outlet or patient report of a disruption.
label: Debunked
why_it_supports: Ochsner's notice (Tier 1) rules it out, and independent outlets report the statement. No source says there was a disruption.
notes: Some outlets' copies of the statement say only “any of our systems”; the notice itself names Epic (MyOchsner/MyChart).

claim_text: A group calling itself Vortex claims it took about 25,000 files from Ochsner's Microsoft 365 environment
summary: KLFY reports a group called Vortex claimed nearly 25,000 files. Acadiana News First and WBRZ, citing a tracker site, report Vortex says it took files from Ochsner's Microsoft 365 system; Acadiana News First adds it seeks payment.
detail: The claim comes from the group's leak-site listing. We did not visit the leak site or any tracker; we cite only the outlets reporting it. KLFY says the claims have not been independently verified. PlayCISO says the listing was posted Nov 19, gives no ransom amount, and notes that some Vortex listings have been reported as unverified or fabricated.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets report the claim; none verifies it, and they trace to one tracker listing.
notes: A claim by an extortion group, relayed by the press. It is not evidence the files were taken.

claim_text: Whether Vortex is behind the Ochsner incident is not established
summary: Ochsner's notice names no attacker and does not mention Vortex. KLFY says Ochsner has not publicly confirmed Vortex was responsible. PlayCISO says the notice and the listing may describe one incident or two.
detail: Both involve Microsoft account data, and the listing appeared the day after Ochsner's Nov 18 determination, but no source shows a link.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No official or independent source ties the group to the incident.
notes: Attribution stays Not established unless Ochsner, a regulator or independent forensic work names an actor.

claim_text: How the two employee accounts were accessed is not established
summary: The notice says two employee accounts were accessed and does not say how: a stolen password, phishing, a missing second login step or something else.
detail: This is the root cause. Nothing in the sources we read describes the method, the accounts' roles or the weakness used.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Ochsner has not said, and The Advocate reports it did not give the employees' roles.
notes: This must be answered before the story can close.

claim_text: How many people are affected is not established
summary: Ochsner says its data review is ongoing and will take additional time. KLFY, WWL-TV and The Advocate all report that no count has been given.
detail: Ochsner will mail letters to people whose information is found to be involved. Whether a count will appear in a federal or state breach filing is not yet known.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Ochsner's own notice (Tier 1) says the review is continuing; no count has been published.

claim_text: Whether any ransom demand was made or any data has been published is not established
summary: KLFY reports Ochsner has not confirmed that the incident involved a ransom demand or that any information has been publicly released. Acadiana News First, citing the tracker, says Vortex is trying to get money from Ochsner.
detail: The ransom claim is the group's, relayed by the press (c005). Ochsner has not confirmed it.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Only the group's own listing, relayed by outlets, speaks to a demand; Ochsner says nothing.

claim_text: Ochsner is offering one year of free credit monitoring to people whose Social Security numbers were involved, and a help line
summary: The notice says people with questions can call a dedicated line on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Central, starting Nov 20, and that formal notice is coming in the coming weeks.
detail: The phone number is on Ochsner's notice; we do not repeat it here.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ochsner's own notice (Tier 1), reported by outlets.

claim_text: Vortex also listed Orlando Health on Nov 19; we found no statement from Orlando Health
summary: PlayCISO reports Vortex named Orlando Health the same day as Ochsner and claims Microsoft 365 files and directory data. It found no statement from Orlando Health as of Nov 20.
detail: This is a related note only. It rests on one analyst post that relays a leak-site listing, and it says nothing about an Ochsner link.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: One Tier 3 analysis relays a claim; no health-system statement or independent confirmation.
notes: Not part of the Ochsner finding.
